text:
The Department of Agricultural & Consumer Economics (ACE) at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (UIUC) is committed to educating decision-makers about global economic issues in food, agriculture, development, environmental sustainability, and financial markets. Our focus on research, education, and extension/outreach, coupled with our commitment to creating an inclusive, welcoming, and supportive work environment, ensures that our esteemed faculty and students can thrive and reach their professional goals.

ACE is excited to invite applications for a tenure-track/tenured open-rank faculty position (Assistant Professor or Associate Professor or Professor) in farm management, agricultural finance, agricultural commodity marketing, agricultural land economics, agricultural law, agricultural industrial organization/supply chains, or domestic rural development. We encourage applications from PhD candidates nearing the completion of their studies, as well as from established scholars.

This open-rank position will help us meet our land-grant university mission, encompassing research, education, and outreach at the nexus of production agriculture in Illinois, with a focus on improving producer decision-making and farm profitability. The incumbent’s Extension and outreach work will include expectations to be an active contributor to the farmdoc project. The incumbent should be agile enough to conduct applied research and extend the results to stakeholders, including farmers, commodity organizations, and policymakers at the local, state, and federal levels. Being available to listen to and engage with stakeholders on their needs will be key.

Possible applied research areas include, but are not limited to, production economics, finance, risk and decision-making, agricultural value/supply chains, and policy analysis. We particularly encourage candidates with demonstrated experience in Extension and/or outreach, working in interdisciplinary teams, and engaging the public on issues relevant to the agricultural sector, securing competitive funding, and mentoring students.

The initial appointment may include research, Extension/outreach, and/or teaching, including online teaching, with stated duties and percentages included in an official offer letter at the time of hiring. The initial appointment will be based upon experience, rank, and department needs, will be determined by the department head, and may evolve over time. We anticipate the initial appointment to be primarily Extension/outreach and that classroom teaching will not exceed one course per year or its equivalent.

Key Responsibilities:
1. Be an active contributor to the farmdoc project, conducting applied research relevant to Illinois stakeholders, including agricultural producers and commodity organizations. Expected activities include writing articles farmdoc daily, development and maintenance of decision-tools, and presentations for stakeholders in both in-person and online (webinar) formats.
2. Direct, two-way engagement with stakeholders to collaboratively identify pressing issues and areas of need to shape and define Extension and outreach activities.
3. Develop and maintain a nationally recognized applied research program to inform their Extension and outreach activities and result in peer-reviewed publications appropriate to the area of research.
4. Collaborate within the Department, College, Illinois Extension, and Campus in developing and delivering innovative and impactful research, education and outreach activities and advance the visions for farmdoc to serve as a model which can extend to other land grant institutions, commodity associations, and federal and state agencies to improve decision-making and profitability for farmers across the country.
5. Seek external funding to support their applied research and outreach programs.
6. The incumbent will be expected to advise, mentor, and potentially fund undergraduate and graduate students in ACE programs.

ACE, the College of Agricultural, Consumer, and Environmental Sciences (ACES), and UIUC campus provide a vibrant and collaborative research and outreach environment. The department hosts the farmdoc project, an award-winning outreach program focused on the economics of Midwest agriculture and supporting stakeholders, including policymakers. farmdoc includes a family of three websites that provide research-based articles, decision tools, and educational videos to agricultural stakeholders in Illinois, across the U.S., and in more than 100 countries. The websites receive over 2 million page views annually, and information is distributed via email campaigns to more than 15,000 subscribers. For more information: https://farmdoc.illinois.edu/about 

ACE and farmdoc have strong partnerships with the Illinois Farm Business Management Association (FBFM) and the major commodity organizations representing Illinois farmers. FBFM comprises over 5,000 cooperating farm families who receive tax management, business planning, and peer benchmarking services from professional field staff throughout the state. These partnerships provide outstanding opportunities to connect directly with stakeholders to provide impactful outreach and research.

At the campus level, the Center for Digital Agriculture (CDA), AI Institute for Future Agricultural Resilience, Management and Sustainability (AIFARMS), I-Illinois Fermentation and Agriculture Biomanufacturing (IFAB), and Institute for Sustainability, Energy, and Environment (iSEE) provide rich opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration.

Minimum Qualifications
1. A terminal degree in agricultural or applied economics, business administration, finance, agricultural law, or a closely related field from an accredited institution, or the ability to complete this terminal degree before starting the position.
2. Demonstrated experience with Extension or outreach activities that could contribute to the farmdoc project.

Preferred Qualifications
1. Familiarity with the mission of land grant institutions and agriculture, as well as familiarity/experience with Extension and outreach.
2. A demonstrated ability to collaborate with departmental faculty, graduate students, and Extension staff in high-impact research and outreach activities.
3. A demonstrated ability or potential to generate external funds to support their research program and graduate students

Salary & Appointment Information:
Competitive, based on qualifications and rank. Starting 9-month salary is in the range of $115,000-$135,000 at the assistant professor level, $135,000-$155,000 at the associate professor level, and $155,000 to $195,000 at the professor level. The initial appointment will be determined by the Department Head and will depend on the incumbent's rank but is expected to be primarily outreach. This position is a full-time, nine-month tenure-track faculty appointment, with the possibility of a summer appointment. This position is eligible for all sponsorship options. The anticipated start date for this position is August 16, 2027.

Application Procedures & Deadline Information
To ensure full consideration, applications must be received by 6:00 pm (CST) on January 6, 2027. However, applications will be accepted until a candidate for hire is identified. Interviews may commence before the closing date, but no offers will be extended until after that date. To apply for this position, use the Apply Now button at the top or bottom of the posting on https://jobs.illinois.edu. Upload a cover letter, a CV, a sample of written work, a maximum of one-page research statement, a maximum of one-page teaching statement, and names and contact information for three references. Providing a sample of Extension work is optional but strongly encouraged. References will not be contacted without the candidate’s permission. All requested information must be submitted via the online system for the application to be considered.

Apply for this position using the Apply Now button at the top or bottom of this posting. Applications not submitted through https://jobs.illinois.edu will not be considered. For further information about this specific position, please contact Nick Paulson, the search committee chair, at npaulson@illinois.edu with “farmdoc faculty” in the subject line. For additional information about the Department, see https://ace.illinois.edu/ or contact Mandy Powell, Administrative Aide, at 217-265-4062, or mandyf@illinois.edu. For questions regarding the application process, please contact 217-333-2137.
